"Learning to Discover Interesting Mathematics"

We define intrinsic interestingness of a theorem as the ratio between the length of its proof and the length of its statement.  They then trained a 27B model to predict proof difficulty and used it to grow a self-expanding library of interesting results. It's a crisp attempt at the question AI math will soon face: which of the millions of provable statements are worth having?

https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.28603
